candidates.label: DDxElement
candidates.comment: A DDxElement is an alternative, closely-related medical condition considered during differential diagnosis, along with the distinguishing signs. Also called differential diagnosis item, alternative diagnosis, rule-out condition. Examples: Considering "strep throat" as a DDxElement for a patient presenting with a sore throat and fever, alongside "common cold."

candidates.label: ListItem
candidates.comment: A ListItem is an intangible representing a single entry within a list, such as a step in a checklist or a how-to description. Also called list entry, item in a sequence, element of a list. Examples: 'Buy milk,' 'Step 1: Preheat oven,' 'First item.' Distinct from ItemList, which is the collection of items.

types.embedding_query_text: Alphabet Examples: Roman letters.

chosen_type.label: Text
chosen_type.justification: Text datatype best approximates an alphabet as a set of characters.

candidates.label: Message
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a single communication from a sender to one or more recipients. Also called communication, dispatch, note, email. Examples: an email, a text message, a direct message on social media, a voicemail.

candidates.label: CssSelectorType
candidates.comment: CssSelectorType is a data type representing a string of text that functions as a CSS selector. Also called CSS selector string, stylesheet selector. Examples: `div.container p`, `#main-content > h1`, `[data-attribute="value"]`.

candidates.label: Text
candidates.comment: A fundamental data type representing a sequence of characters. Also called string, character data, plain text. Examples: "Hello World", "123 Main St", "product description".

candidates.label: Manuscript
candidates.comment: A creative work, such as a book, document, or musical piece, written by hand rather than typed or printed. Also called handwritten document, original script, autograph. Examples: a medieval illuminated manuscript, an author's handwritten draft of a novel, a composer's original musical score.

candidates.label: Language
candidates.comment: Language is an intangible representing natural languages such as Spanish or English, distinct from programming languages. Also called natural tongue, human language, spoken language. Examples: English, Spanish, Mandarin, Arabic. Distinct from ComputerLanguage, which refers to programming languages.

types.embedding_query_text: PageCount Examples: 408 pages.

chosen_type.label: PageCount
chosen_type.definition: PageCount is a numeric value indicating the number of pages in a document or book.
chosen_type.justification: No suitable class for page count; minted PageCount subclass of InteractionCounter.

candidates.label: InteractionCounter
candidates.comment: An InteractionCounter is a structured value summarizing how users have interacted with a CreativeWork. Also called engagement metric, user interaction count, activity tracker. Examples: number of likes, view count, comment count, share count.

candidates.label: BackgroundNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle that provides historical context, definitions, or detailed explanations on a specific topic. Also called explainer article, backgrounder, FAQ document. Examples: "An explainer on climate change", "A detailed history of the European Union", "FAQ about blockchain technology". Distinct from NewsArticle, which reports on current events.

candidates.label: BookFormatType
candidates.comment: An Enumeration representing the physical or digital publication format of a book. Also called book edition type, publication format, reading format. Examples: "Hardcover", "Paperback", "Ebook", "Audiobook".

candidates.label: SearchResultsPage
candidates.comment: A web page displaying the results of a search query. Also called search results, SERP, query results page. Examples: Google search results page, Amazon product search results, a library catalog search page.

candidates.label: HealthAspectEnumeration
candidates.comment: HealthAspectEnumeration is an enumeration of various aspects of health content, used to describe specific facets of health topics online. Also called health content categories, medical information facets, wellness topic types. Examples: 'Symptoms', 'Treatments', 'Causes', 'Prevention'.

types.embedding_query_text: DocumentForm Examples: handwritten book.

chosen_type.label: Manuscript
chosen_type.justification: Manuscript matches handwritten book form.

candidates.label: Manuscript
candidates.comment: A creative work, such as a book, document, or musical piece, written by hand rather than typed or printed. Also called handwritten document, original script, autograph. Examples: a medieval illuminated manuscript, an author's handwritten draft of a novel, a composer's original musical score.

candidates.label: NoteDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A NoteDigitalDocument, as a DigitalDocument, is a file containing a note, primarily for the author's reference. Also called digital note, electronic memo, text note. Examples: a personal reminder in a digital format, a draft of an idea, a quick thought saved electronically. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is intended for public consumption.

candidates.label: BookFormatType
candidates.comment: An Enumeration representing the physical or digital publication format of a book. Also called book edition type, publication format, reading format. Examples: "Hardcover", "Paperback", "Ebook", "Audiobook".

candidates.label: Book
candidates.comment: A CreativeWork consisting of a written or printed work, typically bound together and protected by a cover. Also called publication, volume, printed matter. Examples: "To Kill a Mockingbird", "The Lord of the Rings", "A textbook on physics". Distinct from BookSeries, which is a collection of books.

candidates.label: DigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A creative work representing an electronic file or document. Also called Electronic document, e-document, digital file, computer file. Examples: A PDF report, a Word document, a spreadsheet, an image file, an e-book. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is a broader category for any creative output.

types.embedding_query_text: Property Examples: incomprehensible.

chosen_type.label: Property
chosen_type.justification: Property is the generic class for attributes.

candidates.label: PropertyValueSpecification
candidates.comment: A PropertyValueSpecification is an Intangible defining the specification for a property's value. Also called value constraint, property definition. Examples: a specification for the allowed range of a numerical property, a definition of valid input for a text field, a schema for a complex property value.

candidates.label: Property
candidates.comment: A Property is an Intangible used to indicate attributes and relationships of some Thing, equivalent to rdf:Property. Also called attribute, characteristic, relation. Examples: "name", "description", "url", "author".

candidates.label: LocationFeatureSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value that specifies a feature of an accommodation, represented as a property-value pair. Also called accommodation feature, amenity detail, property value specification. Examples: "hasWifi: true", "numberOfBedrooms: 3", "petsAllowed: false", "poolType: outdoor".

candidates.label: PropertyValue
candidates.comment: A PropertyValue is a StructuredValue representing a property-value pair, such as a feature of a product or place. Also called feature, attribute value, characteristic. Examples: "color: red", "weight: 5kg", "hasWifi: true", "engineType: V8". Distinct from using specific schema.org properties directly, which is preferred when available.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

types.embedding_query_text: Treatment Examples: drinking several glasses of high-quality red wine, fermenting a nutmeg in some dough to combat dysentery.

chosen_type.label: Treatment
chosen_type.definition: A treatment is a method or intervention used to alleviate or cure a health condition.
chosen_type.justification: No candidate fits treatment; minted Treatment subclass of DietarySupplement.

candidates.label: Distillery
candidates.comment: A Distillery is a FoodEstablishment that produces alcoholic beverages through distillation. Also called liquor producer, spirits manufacturer, alcohol plant. Examples: Jack Daniel's Distillery, The Macallan Distillery, Absolut Vodka Distillery. Distinct from Brewery, which produces beer through fermentation.

candidates.label: DietarySupplement
candidates.comment: A product taken orally that contains dietary ingredients intended to supplement the diet, such as vitamins, minerals, or herbs. Also called Nutritional supplement, health supplement, vitamin, herbal remedy. Examples: Multivitamin pills, fish oil capsules, protein powder, ginseng extract. Distinct from Drug, which is primarily for treating, preventing, or diagnosing disease.

candidates.label: BarOrPub
candidates.comment: A FoodEstablishment that primarily serves alcoholic beverages and often food. Also called bar, pub, tavern, lounge. Examples: "The Green Dragon Pub", "O'Malley's Bar & Grill", "The Corner Taproom". Distinct from Restaurant, which primarily focuses on serving meals.

candidates.label: Winery
candidates.comment: A local business that produces wine, often including facilities for grape cultivation, wine production, and tasting. Also called vineyard, wine producer, wine estate. Examples: Robert Mondavi Winery, a local family-owned vineyard, a wine tasting room.

candidates.label: Recipe
candidates.comment: A Recipe is a HowTo CreativeWork providing instructions for preparing food or drink, often noting dietary restrictions. Also called cooking instructions, food preparation guide, culinary formula. Examples: a recipe for chocolate chip cookies, a vegan lasagna recipe, a cocktail recipe, a recipe for homemade bread.

types.embedding_query_text: Tool Examples: AI chatbot.

chosen_type.label: WebAPI
chosen_type.justification: WebAPI represents a software service used as a tool.

candidates.label: ComputerLanguage
candidates.comment: A formal language used for computer programming or other computer representations. Also called programming language, coding language, machine language. Examples: Python, Java, C++, SQL, HTML, XML. Distinct from Language, which refers to natural human languages.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

candidates.label: Conversation
candidates.comment: A series of one or more messages exchanged between individuals or organizations on a specific topic. Also called discussion, dialogue, chat, discourse. Examples: An email thread, a text message exchange, a forum discussion, a spoken dialogue. Distinct from Comment, which is a single remark on an item.

candidates.label: WebAPI
candidates.comment: An application programming interface that is accessible over web or internet technologies. Also called web service, API, REST API. Examples: the Google Maps API, the Twitter API, a weather data API.

candidates.label: UserInteraction
candidates.comment: An outdated general type representing any interaction a user has with a web page or content. Also called user activity, user engagement, web interaction. Examples: a user clicking a link, submitting a form, scrolling a page.

types.embedding_query_text: Correction Examples: expert corrections.

chosen_type.label: CorrectionComment
chosen_type.justification: CorrectionComment directly models correction notes.

candidates.label: CorrectionComment
candidates.comment: A CorrectionComment is a specific type of comment that provides corrections or amendments to a CreativeWork. Also called erratum, amendment, revision note. Examples: A correction notice on an online article, an errata sheet for a book, a revised caption for an image.

candidates.label: AnalysisNewsArticle
candidates.comment: An AnalysisNewsArticle is a NewsArticle that combines factual reporting with the author's expertise, offering interpretations and conclusions. Also called news analysis, interpretive news, expert commentary. Examples: An article analyzing the economic impact of a new policy, a piece interpreting election results, a report on scientific findings with expert commentary. Distinct from NewsArticle, which primarily focuses on factual reporting without extensive interpretation.

candidates.label: ReviewNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A specialized news article that combines factual reporting with a professional critic's assessment of a service, product, performance, or artistic work. Also called critical news report, professional review article, news critique. Examples: a New York Times review of a Broadway show, a tech blog's assessment of a new smartphone, a music magazine's album critique.

candidates.label: MediaManipulationRatingEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of codes used to indicate the authenticity of a media object in the context of its publication or sharing, especially regarding manipulation. Also called media authenticity rating, manipulation type, content integrity code. Examples: "original media", "transformed media", "edited media", "staged media", "misleading context".

candidates.label: BackgroundNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle that provides historical context, definitions, or detailed explanations on a specific topic. Also called explainer article, backgrounder, FAQ document. Examples: "An explainer on climate change", "A detailed history of the European Union", "FAQ about blockchain technology". Distinct from NewsArticle, which reports on current events.

types.embedding_query_text: DocumentCollection Examples: 400 mysterious postcards.

chosen_type.label: ArchiveComponent
chosen_type.justification: ArchiveComponent can represent a collection of archival items.

candidates.label: ProductCollection
candidates.comment: A ProductCollection is a Collection of products, either ProductGroups or specific variants, listed together, often within an Offer. Also called product assortment, product bundle, product set. Examples: a collection of books by an author, a bundle of software products, a set of kitchen utensils, a curated selection of wines.

candidates.label: ArchiveComponent
candidates.comment: An ArchiveComponent is an intangible CreativeWork representing any content within an archive, whether an individual item or a collection, described by specific archival properties. Also called archival item, archival record, archive content, collection item. Examples: a historical letter, a collection of photographs, a government document series, a digital archive file.

candidates.label: PublicationVolume
candidates.comment: A PublicationVolume is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or multi-volume work, often numbered and potentially spanning a time period. Also called journal volume, book volume, periodical volume. Examples: "Nature" Volume 500; "Encyclopedia Britannica" Volume 1; a year's collection of a magazine. Distinct from PublicationIssue, which is a smaller, more granular part of a volume.

candidates.label: PresentationDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A PresentationDigitalDocument is a DigitalDocument file containing slides or used for a presentation. Also called slide deck, presentation file, slideshow. Examples: a Microsoft PowerPoint file, a Google Slides presentation, a Keynote document, a PDF of presentation slides.

candidates.label: MerchantReturnEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of various kinds of product return policies offered by merchants. Also called return policy type, refund option, merchandise return category. Examples: "NoReturns", "FreeReturns", "ReturnsWithFee", "ExchangeOnly".

types.embedding_query_text: Task Examples: transcription and decipherment.

chosen_type.label: Task
chosen_type.definition: A task is an activity performed to achieve a specific goal, such as transcription or decipherment.
chosen_type.justification: No candidate fits generic task; minted Task subclass of ReadAction.

candidates.label: ReadAction
candidates.comment: ReadAction is a ConsumeAction representing the act of consuming written content. Also called reading, perusing, reviewing text. Examples: reading a book, reading an article online, reading an email, reading a newspaper.

candidates.label: Manuscript
candidates.comment: A creative work, such as a book, document, or musical piece, written by hand rather than typed or printed. Also called handwritten document, original script, autograph. Examples: a medieval illuminated manuscript, an author's handwritten draft of a novel, a composer's original musical score.

candidates.label: HowToSection
candidates.comment: A HowToSection is a creative work representing a sub-grouping of steps within a larger HowTo guide. Also called instruction chapter, procedural segment, how-to module. Examples: 'Preparing the Dough' in a bread recipe, 'Connecting the Wires' in an electronics manual.

candidates.label: MusicRecording
candidates.comment: A MusicRecording, as a CreativeWork, is a recorded performance of a musical composition, usually a single song. Also called music track, song recording, audio track. Examples: 'Yesterday' by The Beatles (the recorded version), a single from an album, a demo track. Distinct from MusicComposition, which is the abstract musical work.

candidates.label: DigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A creative work representing an electronic file or document. Also called Electronic document, e-document, digital file, computer file. Examples: A PDF report, a Word document, a spreadsheet, an image file, an e-book. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is a broader category for any creative output.
